items.title: John E. Wood Interview, 1986-06-26
items.q: And then Albert Burbank was with them quite a bit. Yeah. And I, whenever I could afford the time and the money, I enjoyed going down and hearing them play very much.

ctx.x: There's. I think we're catching the feeling of, of, uh, the grapevine that goes on. That I'll see somebody who works with refrigerators for Sears, who's a bass drummer. Yeah. And, uh, you'll run into Greg and is that and the other thing.

It's been interesting to come back and to find that there is as much music as there is. Uh, I, I think, uh, there may, may have been more, I'm sure there was more in the fifties than I was really aware of. Uh, I did not enjoy Bourbon Street music much in the fifties, although, as I may have told you before, I used to, to go to the Paddock Lounge and hear the Bill Matthews Band, which I guess, again, was a band whose members change right much from time to time. But, it frequently had him and Albert, always had him…
What about the big dance halls?
